title: Agent Archivist shared wire vocabulary (v1)
description: Primitive shapes, identifier grammars, and the closed v1 enum sets shared by the ingest wire schema family (docs/notes/wire-schemas.md). Every enum here is fail-closed on unknown values per plan Section 7.1; the `x-archivist.bearing` metadata records which enums are security- or identity-bearing. Every numeric shape is an integer: protocol structures contain no floating-point values.

uuid-v4.description: Random UUID in lowercase canonical text (plan Section 7.4): tenant, client, and adapter-minted synthetic session identifiers.

uuid-v7.description: Time-ordered UUID in lowercase canonical text (plan Section 7.4): generation and request identifiers, frozen when the spool entry is created so retries reproduce them.

sha256-hex.description: Lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest: blob digests, derived identifier hashes, checksums, and key identifiers.

ed25519-signature-hex.description: Lowercase hexadecimal Ed25519 signature (64 raw bytes).

ed25519-public-key-hex.description: Lowercase hexadecimal Ed25519 public key (32 raw bytes). Public halves only: verification material travels by value where a record must verify offline (the receipt certificate); private keys never appear in any schema, file, or argument (SEC-006).

key-id.description: Ed25519 key identifier: the lowercase-hex SHA-256 of the encoded public key. Identifies uploader authorization keys and receipt-signing keys; derivation is pinned so key IDs are computable from any published public record.

short-token.description: Bounded lowercase token (plan Section 7.4 harness grammar): harness IDs, adapter IDs, enum-like tokens that become object-key segments.

version-token.description: Bounded version token (the error-message `version` charset): adapter projection versions and similar software-version labels carried in provenance.

opaque-id.description: Opaque UTF-8 identifier (plan Section 7.4): upstream session, adapter artifact, and correlation identifiers. At most 1,024 bytes; never case-folded, never Unicode-normalized, never trimmed — lookalikes stay distinct sessions. `maxLength` is the codepoint superset; the byte bound in `x-archivist.byteMaxLength` is the normative limit.

rfc3339-utc-timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC (`Z` suffix only; plan Section 7.3: persisted timestamps are RFC 3339 UTC and local time is a display choice). Calendar validity and range sanity are server-side validation (VAL-002), not syntax.

u63.description: Non-negative integer below 2^63. Every wire integer uses this shape: no floats exist anywhere in protocol structures, and values stay renderable by the error-message integer placeholders.

artifact-kind.description: Artifact kind (plan Section 7.3): `file-slice` is an exact complete-record byte slice of a file source; `database-projection` is a versioned allowlisted projection of database events. Identity-bearing: the kind is an input to the artifact hash, so an unknown value fails closed.

range-kind.description: Range coordinate kind (plan Section 7.4 occurrence inputs). `byte` ranges address offsets into a source byte stream; `event` ranges address projected-event ordinals. Identity-bearing: an input to the occurrence hash, so an unknown value fails closed.

id-source.description: Origin of the upstream session identifier (plan Section 7.4): `upstream` was read from the harness; `synthetic` is an adapter-minted UUIDv4 standing in for a missing harness session ID, never inferred from a path name. Identity-bearing: an unknown value fails closed.

storage-profile.description: Named canonical storage encoder (plan Sections 7.5 and 7.6): `zstd-v1` is Zstandard level 3, single-threaded, no dictionary, content size and checksum enabled, with the encoder dependency pinned for the life of the profile. A new canonical encoder requires a new named profile and prefix; it never rewrites the meaning of `zstd-v1`. Security-bearing: determines stored bytes and key prefixes, so an unknown value fails closed.

transport-encoding.description: Declared wire encoding of the payload part (plan Section 7.6: the client may transport canonical bytes raw or with a declared transport encoding; the server decodes exactly one declared encoding per request). `identity` carries the canonical bytes unchanged; `zstd` carries one Zstandard frame of the canonical bytes at any legal level — it is a transport convenience only, distinct from the `zstd-v1` storage profile the server produces. Security-bearing: a misdeclared encoding changes what the server decodes, so an unknown value fails closed.

checksum-algorithm.description: Algorithm of the envelope's incoming representation checksum. SHA-256 only in v1. Security-bearing: an unknown value fails closed rather than being guessed.

storage-outcome.description: Per-object storage outcome (plan Section 7.7; RCPT-003): exactly what the backend can establish, never stronger. `already_present` requires readable compatible metadata; a writer-only overwrite profile reports the weaker unknown-physical result. Security-bearing: deduplication honesty, so an unknown value fails closed.

signature-algorithm.description: Digital signature algorithm for request authorization and receipts. Ed25519 only in v1. Security-bearing: an unknown value fails closed.

blob-object-key.description: Server-derived raw blob key (plan Section 7.5), assembled only from the validated tenant UUID, the pinned profile, and the computed canonical digest. The two-hex segment is the digest shard.

occurrence-object-key.description: Server-derived occurrence key (plan Section 7.5): tenant, origin client, harness, session shard, session hash, occurrence hash. Raw upstream identifiers are hashed in, never embedded. The two-hex segment is the session-hash shard.

attestation-object-key.description: Server-derived upload-attestation key (plan Section 7.5): tenant, occurrence shard, occurrence hash, attestation hash.
